A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, if we want to control a network, it is better to control a few nodes and to use an average output rather than to control each node individually.
the proposed approach allows to reduce the computational burden of the control design and the robustness of the control system.
, for a given number of controlled nodes, it is more convenient to choose the output as the average of the nodes than to choose the nodes which are more important in the network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for large scale networks, controlling the output of the network can be a good strategy to reduce the control complexity.
the control problem for large scale networks is much more tractable if one considers an output instead of the whole system.
the Output Controllablity approach is a very useful and powerful tool to study and control large scale network systems.
